historical_references.reference: Verina, the daughter of Justinian I, was a Byzantine empress who ruled as regent during the minority of her son, Justin II. She came to power in 548 AD and reigned until 552 AD. Her rule was marked by military successes against the Persians and the Goths, as well as internal unrest and rebellion.

Verina, a Christian saint, was the mother of St. Leander of Seville. She is believed to have lived in the late 5th or early 6th century AD and is venerated in the Roman Catholic Church and the Anglican Communion. Her life and deeds are not well documented, but she is remembered for her piety and her role in the education and spiritual growth of her son.
